messages.content:
You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE conductor (
    Conductor_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Age INT,
    Nationality TEXT,
    Year_of_Work INT,
    UNIQUE (Conductor_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE orchestra (
    Orchestra_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Orchestra TEXT,
    Conductor_ID INT,
    Record_Company TEXT,
    Year_of_Founded REAL,
    Major_Record_Format TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Orchestra_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Conductor_ID) REFERENCES conductor(Conductor_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE performance (
    Performance_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Orchestra_ID INT,
    Type TEXT,
    Date TEXT,
    Official_ratings_(millions) REAL,
    Weekly_rank TEXT,
    Share TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Performance_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Orchestra_ID) REFERENCES orchestra(Orchestra_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE show (
    Show_ID INT,
    Performance_ID INT,
    If_first_show bool,
    Result TEXT,
    Attendance REAL,
    FOREIGN KEY (Performance_ID) REFERENCES performance(Performance_ID)
);

There isn’t a “famous” flag/column in your schema, so you’ll need to define what “famous” means (e.g., most performances, highest ratings, biggest attendance, most orchestras, etc.).

If you just want a list of conductors:

```sql
SELECT Conductor_ID, Name, Age, Nationality, Year_of_Work
FROM conductor
ORDER BY Name;
```

If you mean “most performed” (conductors whose orchestras have the most performances):

```sql
SELECT c.Conductor_ID, c.Name, COUNT(p.Performance_ID) AS performance_count
FROM conductor c
JOIN orchestra o ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
ORDER BY performance_count DESC;
```

How do you want to define “famous” in this database?
I want the names of conductors that meet those criteria.

Which criteria do you mean—“most performed” (most performances), “highest rated” (max/avg `Official_ratings_(millions)`), or “biggest attendance” (from `show.Attendance`)?

If you meant **most performed**, here are the **names** (optionally top N):

```sql
-- Names of conductors ordered by number of performances (most to least)
SELECT c.Name
FROM conductor c
JOIN orchestra o ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC;
```

If you want only the **top 10**:

```sql
SELECT c.Name
FROM conductor c
JOIN orchestra o ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
only consider conductors who have conducted multiple orchestras, not just one.

```sql
SELECT c.Name
FROM conductor c
JOIN orchestra o ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.Orchestra_ID) > 1
ORDER BY c.Name;
```
I only want conductors based on their past conducting activities, like how many orchestras they worked with.

```sql
-- Conductors who have worked with multiple orchestras, ranked by how many
SELECT
  c.Name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.Orchestra_ID) AS orchestras_worked_with
FROM conductor c
JOIN orchestra o ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.Orchestra_ID) > 1
ORDER BY orchestras_worked_with DESC, c.Name;
```
